definitions.explanation: Describes something that catches one's interest because it is rare or unfamiliar. Often implies looking at something with wide-eyed curiosity, as if encountering it for the first time.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちは{物珍|ものめずら}しそうに{見|み}ていた。
examples.english: The children were watching with curiosity.

examples.japanese: {外国|がいこく}の{食|た}べ{物|もの}が{物珍|ものめずら}しくて{色々|いろいろ}{試|ため}した。
examples.english: I was curious about foreign foods and tried all sorts of things.

examples.japanese: {最初|さいしょ}は{物珍|ものめずら}しかった{田舎|いなか}の{生活|せいかつ}にもすっかり{慣|な}れた。
examples.english: I've gotten completely used to rural life, which at first seemed so novel.

notes:
USAGE:
{物珍|ものめずら}しい often appears in the adverbial form {物珍|ものめずら}しそうに ("as if finding something novel") to describe the way someone looks at or reacts to something unfamiliar. The nuance is lighter than {珍|めずら}しい alone, emphasizing the curiosity of the observer.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {物珍|ものめずら}しそうに{見|み}る (to look at with curiosity)
- {物珍|ものめずら}しさ (novelty, unfamiliarity)
- {物珍|ものめずら}しい{目|め}で{見|み}る (to look at with curious eyes)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{珍|めずら}しい is the more common and general word for "rare" or "unusual." {物珍|ものめずら}しい specifically emphasizes the viewer's sense of novelty and curiosity.
